question: does grouped prefill + the fp16 result wire change output quality?
why_the_obvious_tests_failed: greedy agreement over 24 tokens: invalid. one flipped token changes every token after it, so it measures divergence, not numerical error. read 57% and panicked; `count` was 24/24 at delta 0.006.
6-prompt top-1 logprob delta: underpowered. the baseline's own 3-pass spread was 0.339 nats, the same size as the effect being measured.
instrument: 120 independent prompts, ~230 words each, one forward pass (max_tokens=1). independent => no greedy divergence. 120 samples => per-prompt nondeterminism averages down.
control: the baseline compared against ITSELF. it is the ceiling: no change can score better than the reference reproducing itself.
verdict: indistinguishable. the baseline disagrees with its own second pass on 11 of 120 prompts; the new stack sits in that band.
not_claimed: this is not proof of numerical equality. it is proof the change is smaller than the nondeterminism it lives in.
incidental_finding: this rig has never been reproducible. the PRE-EXISTING per-route GEMV path flips argmax on 9% of prompts run twice, and its 3-pass top-1 spread (0.339) is WIDER than the grouped path's (0.277). not introduced today.
